sop_title: FCC Government Purchase Card Program: Issuance, Purchasing, Reconciliation, Disputes, Review, and Account Closure
summary: This SOP covers the FCC purchase card lifecycle: nominating and training cardholders and Approving Officials, issuing cards and changing limits, authorizing and making purchases, reconciling monthly Statements of Account (SOAs), disputing charges, reviewing accounts, and closing them. It is run by cardholders, Approving Officials (AOs), Bureau/Office Chiefs, the Agency Program Coordinator (APC), and the Financial Operations Center (FOC) RDG/TOG under the CFO, with support from the Enterprise Acquisition Center (EAC) and oversight by auditors and the OIG.

steps.action: Nominates employees as cardholders and AOs for the organization.
steps.input: Organizational need for purchase card holder or AO
steps.source_quote: Nominating cardholders and AOs for their respective organizations

steps.action: Completes GSA purchase card web-based training.
steps.source_quote: must complete the General Services Administration (GSA) purchase card web-based training prior to issuance

steps.action: Completes and signs Form A-498, certifying they have read and understand the directive.
steps.source_quote: must complete and sign Form A-498

steps.action: Signs the cardholder nominee's Form A-498.
steps.source_quote: signed by their Bureau/Office Chief (or Assistant Bureau Chief (ABC) for Management if applicable) and their AO

steps.action: Signs the cardholder nominee's Form A-498.
steps.input: Form A-498 signed by nominee and AO
steps.source_quote: signed by their Bureau/Office Chief (or Assistant Bureau Chief (ABC) for Management if applicable) and their AO

steps.action: Submits the bank card application form, training certificate, and signed Form A-498 to FOC RDG/TOG.
steps.input: Bank card application; training certificate; signed Form A-498
steps.system: Bank card application form; Form A-498
steps.source_quote: submit a completed bank card application form to FOC, RDG/TOG

steps.action: Submits the training certificate of completion to the APC.
steps.output: Training certificate on file with APC
steps.source_quote: Submit a certificate of completion of cardholder training (the same training required of purchase cardholder nominees) to the APC

steps.action: Submits the cardholder's bank card application to the contractor bank.
steps.source_quote: for submission to the contractor bank

steps.action: Issues the purchase card and opens the cardholder account.
steps.input: Approved application; training certificate; signed Form A-498
steps.source_quote: issues and destroys cards; opens and closes accounts

steps.action: Submits a written request and justification to the APC for a permanent single transaction limit increase up to the MPT.
steps.source_quote: upon written request and justification provided by the respective cardholder's AO

steps.action: Submits Form A-1204 to the APC to request a monthly credit limit increase.
steps.input: Cardholder need for a higher monthly limit
steps.source_quote: Submit a written request via FCC Form A-1204 Request for Monthly Credit Limit Increase to the APC

steps.action: Grants the limit increase and retains the circumstances and the duration (temporary or permanent).
steps.output: Increased limit; retained record of circumstances and duration
steps.source_quote: A cardholder's monthly credit limit may be increased by the APC

steps.action: Periodically reviews permanent monthly credit limit increases to determine whether they are still required.
steps.source_quote: Permanent monthly credit limit increases shall be reviewed by the APC on a periodic basis

steps.action: Provides the cardholder with written authorization for each transaction before the purchase.
steps.source_quote: Provide written authorization (such as through a memo, note, or e-mail) to the cardholder for each purchase card transaction before the purchase is made

steps.action: Ensures funds are available before initiating the purchase.
steps.output: Funds availability confirmed; funding document reference
steps.source_quote: Ensure availability of funds prior to initiating a purchase with the card

steps.action: Considers mandatory Government priority sources under FAR Part 8 before other sources.
steps.source_quote: Cardholders shall adhere to the priorities for use of mandatory Government sources in FAR Part 8

steps.action: Reviews the purchase terms and conditions for prohibited provisions (recurring payments, automatic renewal, unlimited duration, indemnification, unlimited liability).
steps.source_quote: Cardholders are responsible for reviewing terms and conditions applicable to any purchase before making the purchase

steps.action: Refers the agreement with prohibited provisions to EAC before making any commitment.
steps.source_quote: Cardholders shall refer all agreements that include such provisions to the Enterprise Acquisition Center (EAC)

steps.action: Establishes a contract that addresses the objectionable terms, consulting OGC as necessary.
steps.source_quote: EAC can establish a contract that addresses the objectionable terms

steps.action: Evaluates whether the price of the goods or services is reasonable.
steps.source_quote: Cardholders must consider the price of goods or services being purchased and only make a purchase if the price is reasonable.

steps.action: Completes any other purchase card forms the AO requires.
steps.source_quote: Complete all other FCC purchase card-related form(s) for each transaction, as instructed by the cardholder's AO

steps.action: Completes and attaches the Section 508 Determination and Findings form for covered IT products or services.
steps.system: Section 508 Determination and Findings for Purchase Requests Form
steps.source_quote: Complete and attach Section 508 Determination and Findings for Purchase Requests Form if the item is covered

steps.action: Initiates the purchase with the merchant (in store, online, or by phone) and confirms the state sales tax exemption is applied at the point of sale.
steps.source_quote: Cardholders should ensure that their purchases have been exempted from state sales tax at the point of sale

steps.action: Validates receipt of the purchased items and signs the receipt or invoice received with the shipment.
steps.source_quote: Validate the receipt of items purchased, as applicable, prior to the cardholder's receipt and shall affix his/her signature on the receipt or invoice

steps.action: Signs and dates the invoice for goods or services they accepted or first used.
steps.output: Invoice signed and dated by receiving employee
steps.source_quote: the cardholder may not reconcile his/her SOA until they have obtained the signature and date of that other employee on the invoice

steps.action: Reconciles the monthly SOA from the contractor bank, signs it with printed name and date, and forwards it to the AO.
steps.source_quote: Cardholders shall reconcile their monthly SOA received from the contractor bank within seven (7) workdays after the end of the billing cycle.

steps.action: Reviews the reconciled SOA to verify the transactions were legal, proper, correct, and necessary, then signs it with printed name and date.
steps.source_quote: AOs shall review each reconciled SOA received from their purchase cardholders within ten (10) workdays after the end of the billing cycle.

steps.action: Forwards the certified reconciled SOA to FOC RDG/TOG.
steps.source_quote: The AO then must forward the reconciled SOA to Financial Operations Center (FOC), Revenue and Disbursement Group (RDG)/Travel and Operations Group (TOG).

steps.action: Ensures the reconciled transaction data is entered into the core financial accounting system and distributes charges to the correct financial and budgetary accounts.
steps.source_quote: ensuring all reconciled purchase card transaction data is entered into the Commission's core financial accounting system

steps.action: Pays the purchase card contractor bank.
steps.source_quote: for paying the purchase card contractor bank

steps.action: Retains the reconciled SOA and all required supporting documentation for six years.
steps.input: Reconciled SOA; authorization; funding reference; invoices; agreements; receipt acknowledgments
steps.source_quote: Cardholders shall retain supporting documentation for purchases for a period of six (6) years.

steps.action: Reviews receipts for a questioned charge, for example a charge posted under a different merchant name.
steps.source_quote: Review the receipts.

steps.action: Contacts the merchant to resolve the disputed charge and documents the actions taken.
steps.source_quote: the cardholder shall contact the merchant in an attempt to resolve the disputed charge

steps.action: Initiates a dispute request with the purchase card contractor bank.
steps.source_quote: the cardholder shall immediately proceed with a dispute request with the purchase card contractor bank

steps.action: Assists the cardholder in resolving the disputed payment.
steps.source_quote: Assist the cardholder in resolving disputed payments

steps.action: Tracks the dispute to completion.
steps.source_quote: Cardholders shall track disputes to completion.

steps.action: Completes GSA refresher training and provides certification to the APC.
steps.input: Refresher training cycle or APC direction
steps.source_quote: take GSA's web-based training as refresher training every three (3) years

steps.action: Reviews purchase card usage to identify accounts with no activity in the preceding three years.
steps.source_quote: the APC will review purchase card usage to identify inactive accounts

steps.action: Provides the list of inactive accounts to each Bureau/Office.
steps.source_quote: The APC will provide a list of inactive accounts to each Bureau/Office

steps.action: Confirms the continued need for each inactive account.
steps.source_quote: the Bureau/Office must confirm the continued need for each inactive account

steps.action: Suspends the inactive account until confirmation is received.
steps.source_quote: Failure to provide the requested confirmation will result in the inactive account's suspension until confirmation is received.

steps.action: Conduct periodic or random reviews of cardholder transactions and purchase practices.
steps.source_quote: Cardholders shall be subject to periodic and/or random reviews of their purchase card transactions

steps.action: Furnishes reconciled SOAs and supporting documentation directly to the reviewers or auditors.
steps.source_quote: cardholders are directly responsible for furnishing copies of their reconciled SOAs and all other supporting documentation

steps.action: Reviews the cardholder's standing in the program, which may lead to temporary suspension or expulsion.
steps.output: Standing decision (suspension, expulsion, or other action)
steps.source_quote: the cardholder's standing in the purchase card program will be subject to review by the APC

steps.action: Reports abuse, misuse, or non-compliance to the cardholder's AO or the AO's immediate supervisor, and may suspend card privileges or AO authority.
steps.source_quote: The APC will report purchase card abuse, misuse, and non-compliance to the cardholder's AO or to the AO's immediate supervisor.

steps.action: Reports misuse or fraud to the immediate supervisor (or ABC), the Chief of HRM Labor Relations and Performance Management, and the OIG.
steps.source_quote: The APC will report purchase card misuse or fraud to the cardholder's or AO's immediate supervisor

steps.action: Takes disciplinary or adverse action with HR Labor Relations and Performance Management in cases of fraud or misuse.
steps.source_quote: Taking appropriate disciplinary or adverse action in conjunction with Human Resources Labor Relations and Performance Management

steps.action: Gives the APC prior written notice of the cardholder's transfer or separation.
steps.output: Notice to APC to cancel the card
steps.source_quote: prior notice shall be given to the APC by the cardholder's AO or Bureau/Office Chief (or ABC if applicable)

steps.action: Provides all purchase card records and supporting documentation to the AO and surrenders the card to the AO or APC before separation or transfer.
steps.output: Records transferred to AO; card surrendered
steps.source_quote: provide all of their purchase card records and supporting documentation to their AO and surrender their purchase card to their AO or the APC

steps.action: Notes on the final reconciled SOA that the departed cardholder could not sign and date it.
steps.input: Final SOA issued after the cardholder's departure
steps.source_quote: the AO shall note this on the cardholder's final reconciled SOA

steps.action: Closes the cardholder's account.
steps.source_quote: the APC shall close the cardholder's account

steps.action: Designates a new AO when an AO separates or transfers, and sends the change in writing to the APC.
steps.output: New AO designation sent to APC
steps.source_quote: a new AO will be designated by the appropriate Bureau/Office Chief (or ABC if applicable)

risks.description: Form A-498 passes from nominee to AO to Bureau/Office Chief (or ABC) and back to the nominee for submission to FOC RDG/TOG (7.F.1). The SOP gives no tracking or deadline for these signature handoffs, so a nomination can stall without anyone noticing.

Section 6.A.4 says training certificates go to the APC. Section 7.F.1 says the cardholder sends the certificate with the application package to FOC RDG/TOG. The SOP does not say who confirms training and a fully signed Form A-498 before the APC issues the card (D1).
If training or a signed Form A-498 is missing, the card is not issued. No next step, owner, or notification back to the nominee is stated.
No handling is stated when the APC denies a single transaction or monthly limit increase, or when a permanent monthly increase is requested for a non-OMD cardholder (6.B.4).
Permanent monthly credit limit increases are reviewed 'on a periodic basis' (6.B.5). No frequency is stated, so elevated limits can stay in place indefinitely.

Per-transaction AO authorization may be a memo, note, or email (7.E.2; 7.F.4). There is no consistent record or tracking, yet a copy must be kept as supporting documentation (6.D) and produced for audit.

The cardholder alone ensures funds are available before purchasing (7.F.5). No independent check is stated, and the SOP warns of a possible Anti-Deficiency Act violation with no stated handling if it happens.
If the price is not reasonable the cardholder does not purchase (6.A.9). No next step is stated, such as seeking another source or consulting EAC.

The AO validates receipt 'as applicable' and 'prior to the cardholder's receipt' (7.E.3). It is unclear which purchases need AO validation and how this relates to the receiving employee signature in S25.

The monthly SOA is reconciled with wet signatures and forwarded cardholder to AO to FOC RDG/TOG (6.C.1–6.C.2). There is no stated tracking of the 7- and 10-workday deadlines or of where each SOA sits.
Each SOA must be certified by the cardholder's AO within 10 workdays. No alternate AO is named for absences; 14.B covers only AO separation or transfer.
Transaction data that originates in the contractor bank's SOA is reconciled on paper and then must be entered into the core financial accounting system (7.B). The same data is keyed again downstream.
The CFO ensures 'timely receipt' of reconciled SOAs from AOs (7.B). No FOC-side deadline or follow-up action for missing SOAs is stated.
Shipping and tax charges can only be resolved with the merchant (12.B). No next step is stated if the merchant refuses the credit.
Only the cardholder tracks disputes against the 90-calendar-day bank window (12.A). No AO or APC monitoring is stated, so the government's interest can be lost when a dispute is missed.
The Bureau/Office must confirm continued need for inactive accounts, but no response deadline or Bureau/Office owner is stated before suspension (6.A.5).
Cardholders must provide audit documentation 'in a timely manner' (6.E.1). No deadline is stated.

The APC closes the account only 'upon being notified' by the AO or Bureau/Office Chief (14.A; 14.C). No independent check against separations or transfers is stated, so a card can stay active after the holder leaves.

Individual cardholders hold six years of purchase records and hand them to the AO on departure (6.D; 14.A). No tracking or confirmation of the transfer is stated, which risks lost records for later audits.
The APC alone issues cards, grants limit increases, suspends accounts, and closes accounts (7.D; 6.B; 6.A.5; 14.C). No backup or delegate is named.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.reason: Chief submits the nomination through a form that starts the nominee package. This replaces informal requests and creates a record.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Apps form writing to a SharePoint 'Card Nominations' list

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.reason: Paper Form A-498 becomes an electronic form with the nominee's certification and training certificate upload. FOC must confirm that electronic signature meets the 'complete and sign' requirement (6.A.3).
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Apps form + SharePoint list with attachments

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.reason: Routes Form A-498 to the AO for sign-off automatically, removing an untracked handoff (R1).
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate with Approvals connector (sequential stage 1)

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.reason: Second stage of the same approval flow routes Form A-498 to the Bureau/Office Chief or ABC after AO approval.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate with Approvals connector (sequential stage 2)

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.reason: Once all approvals are recorded, a flow checks that the training certificate and fully signed A-498 are present and sends the package to FOC RDG/TOG. This also gives D1 an explicit check (R2, R3).
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate (SharePoint + Outlook connectors)

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.reason: AO nominees upload training certificates to a central training register instead of emailing the APC, so certificates are retrievable for review.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Apps form writing to a SharePoint 'Training Register' list

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.reason: The written single transaction limit increase request and justification is captured in a structured form routed to the APC.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Apps form + SharePoint 'Limit Requests' list

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.reason: Form A-1204 becomes an electronic form. Requested amount, circumstances, and temporary or permanent duration are stored as fields, which the APC must retain (6.B.4).
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Apps form + SharePoint 'Limit Requests' list

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.reason: Granting limit increases is an APC judgment on demonstrated need and on the OMD-only rule for permanent monthly increases.
recommendations.suggested_tool: None (APC records decision in SharePoint list)

recommendations.label: automate

recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate Recurrence trigger + SharePoint + Planner/Outlook

recommendations.label: digitize

recommendations.label: keep_human

recommendations.label: digitize

starter_flows.trigger: When an item is created in the SharePoint 'Purchase Authorizations' list (submitted from the Power Apps purchase request form).
actions: Get the cardholder's record from the 'Cardholder Register' list (AO, single transaction limit, account status).
Condition: account status is Active. If not, notify the cardholder and set request status to 'Rejected - account not active'.
Condition: requested amount is at or below the cardholder's single transaction limit (6.B.2). If above, notify the cardholder and set status to 'Rejected - exceeds limit'.
Check that the funding document reference field is populated. If empty, return the request to the cardholder.
If the Section 508 flag is Yes, check that a Section 508 D&F attachment exists. If missing, return the request to the cardholder.
Start and wait for an approval (AO).
Update the item with outcome, AO name, comments, and approval timestamp.
Email the cardholder the authorization outcome with a link to the record; it serves as the retained authorization copy (6.D).
starter_flows.approval_step: AO approves or rejects the purchase before it is made (7.E.2; 7.F.4).

starter_flows.trigger: When an item in the SharePoint 'SOA Reconciliations' list is modified and Status equals 'Cardholder Certified'.
actions: Get the cardholder's AO from the 'Cardholder Register' list.
Calculate the 10-workday AO deadline from the billing cycle end date stored on the item.
Start an approval (AO) with a link to the reconciled SOA and attached receipts and invoices, plus a field for Certification Clause exceptions (6.C.4).
